data.title: Undo of a history delete goes through add(): the newest-entry dedupe deletes a different entry, and the restored entry jumps to the top
data.scenario: The history page's Undo (lib/history/view/history_page.dart:66) calls cubit.add(entry), and HistoryRepository.add applies the 'replace newest if same text+target+engine' rule. Reproduced with a MemoryStore: add old('Hello'->'Bonjour', fr, google), add mid('Bye'), add new('Hello'->'Salut', same target and engine). Then delete('old') followed by add(old), which is what Undo does. The result is [old:Bonjour, mid], so the newer 'Salut' entry is silently lost. Even when nothing matches, an undone old entry comes back at the top instead of its original place (reproduced: [old, c, b]), and at the cap the restore can evict another entry.
data.fix: Add a dedicated HistoryRepository.restore(entry) / HistoryCubit.restore(entry) that inserts the entry at its createdAt position, applies no newest-entry dedupe and does not remove other ids. Use it for Undo instead of add().

- The Undo action at lines 67-68 calls `cubit.add(entry)`.

data.title: The newest-entry dedupe overwrites a favourite's saved translation, and it ignores source language and options
data.scenario: _sameRequest compares only trimmed text, target and engineId, and the replacement keeps the favourite flag but takes the new translation. Reproduced: add favourite {text:'How are you', target de, engine ai:x, translation 'Wie geht es Ihnen?'}, then add the same text with translation "Wie geht's dir?". The result is a single favourite holding "Wie geht's dir?"; the formal translation the user starred is gone. Ordinary flows trigger this: (1) star a translation, then tap a refinement chip ('Make it shorter'); (2) star an alternative or variation, then tap it in History, which calls setInputAndTranslate and re-translates; (3) re-translate with an AI engine or after changing formality. Because source is ignored, 'gift' en->de followed by 'gift' no->de also collapses into one entry (reproduced: only 'no:Gift' remains).
data.fix: Only merge into the newest entry when it is not a favourite, or when the translation is unchanged. Otherwise insert a new entry. Add source to _sameRequest. If alternatives/variations still need to update the entry in place, give them an explicit update-by-id path rather than relying on add().

data.title: Typing refinements are not deduplicated, so instant translate fills history with prefixes and evicts real entries
data.scenario: The class doc says the dedupe covers 'typing refinements', but _sameRequest needs exact text equality. Instant translate is on by default for Mozhi engines (600 ms debounce), and every completed debounced result is recorded (TranslateCubit._onResult -> _record). Typing 'Good morning' with short pauses therefore stores 'Good', 'Good mor' and 'Good morning' as three entries. Reproduced: add('Good'), add('Good mor'), add('Good morning') returns all three. Over time these fragments use up the 1000-entry cap and push out real history.
data.fix: In add(), also replace the newest entry when it is not a favourite, has the same source, target and engine, was created within a short window (for example 30 s), and either trimmed text is a prefix of the other (or the edit distance is small). Keep the exact-match rule as well.

'Good', 'Good mor' and 'Good morning' never match each other, so each is stored at the front as a new entry (line 44). The class doc (lines 9-10) says this covers "(typing refinements)", but exact equality cannot do that.

data.title: Un-starring an old favourite when history is at the cap deletes it at once, with no way to re-star
data.scenario: toggleFavorite runs through _mutate, which applies _capped. With maxEntries=2 (in production, 1000 newer non-favourites): add favourite 'old', add n1, add n2, then toggleFavorite('old') returns [n2, n1], and 'old' is permanently removed from storage. A heavy user who un-stars an old favourite from the Favourites filter sees it vanish and cannot tap the star again to undo.
data.fix: Do not apply the cap in toggleFavorite (cap only in add/importJson), or exempt the entry being toggled until the next add, so the action can be reversed. Alternatively, offer an undo snackbar that restores the favourite flag.

data.title: A transient prefs read error is treated as 'nothing stored'; the next mutation overwrites the real settings and orphans API keys
data.scenario: _readSettings swallows every exception and returns null, so load() returns const AppSettings(), and the test 'returns defaults when the preferences fail' encodes this. Reproduced with a store whose reads throw once: load() returns 0 providers and onboardingComplete=false. The user sees onboarding, any change triggers save(), and _save (its previous read also fails, and _knownProviderIds is empty) writes the default JSON over the real one. After restart the reads work again: providers=0, onboardingComplete=false and the instance list is reset, while 'apikey.a' stays orphaned in secure storage.
data.fix: Distinguish 'absent' or 'corrupt' from 'read failed'. Let load() rethrow (or return a flag) on storage errors so bootstrap can retry or keep the app read-only. In _save, do not overwrite settings.v1 when the previous read threw, and do not treat that case as 'no previous providers'.

data.title: Orphan API-key cleanup only knows ids from the stored JSON or this session, so some secrets stay in secure storage forever
data.scenario: _save finds stale keys only from _knownProviderIds and the provider ids in the previous settings.v1. Any apikey.<id> whose id is no longer listed is never deleted. Reproduced: prefs hold default settings and secrets hold {'apikey.gone': 'sk-gone'}; after load() and save(), the secret is still there. Real ways to get there: the app is killed after prefs.write(settingsKey) but before secrets.delete for a provider the user just removed; on iOS, Keychain items survive uninstall while prefs do not, so keys from an earlier install are never cleaned; a provider element that AppSettings.fromJson drops; the read failure in data-5. The user believes the key was deleted, but it remains on the device.
data.fix: Keep an index of stored key ids inside the secret store (for example an 'apikey.index' JSON list) and use it as the source of stale ids. Alternatively, delete the keys of removed providers before writing the new JSON. On first run, with no settings.v1 present, clear any leftover apikey.* entries listed in the index.

data.title: History has no size limit and is rewritten as one prefs string; on web, filling the quota stops all history writes and breaks settings saves
data.scenario: Only the entry count is capped; text and translation length are unbounded (translate input has no maxLength). _mutate re-encodes the whole list into one value under history.v1, in the same SharedPreferencesAsync/localStorage that holds settings.v1. On web (about 5 MB localStorage quota), translating long texts (around 20-40 KB per entry, roughly 100-200 entries) makes store.write throw QuotaExceededError. From then on every add() fails, because the eviction is computed only in memory and never written. History silently stops recording (the errors only reach addError and the log). A settings change that makes settings.v1 larger, such as adding a provider or pinning a language, also fails to persist.
data.fix: Cap the stored text and translation per entry (or the total encoded size) and evict the oldest non-favourites until under a byte budget. On a write failure, evict more and retry. Consider a separate storage backend for history so it cannot starve settings.
data.verifierNotes:
The bug is real, but only on web, and the trigger is uncommon.

What the code confirms:
- lib/history/data/history_repository.dart:95-100. `_capped` limits only how many non-favourite entries are kept (default `maxEntries = 1000`, line 16). Nothing limits size. HistoryEntry (lib/history/models/history_entry.dart) stores the full `text` and `translation` with no truncation.
- No `maxLength` or LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter appears anywhere in lib/translate, and `_record` (translate_cubit.dart:599-618) stores `request.text` and `result.text` unchanged. cubit.title: If the saved engine's language list fails to load, every engine is unusable, even after Retry and across restarts
cubit.scenario: loadEngines always picks the saved engine first (settings.engineId), and if that engine's language list fails to load, nothing else is tried. The catch only emits enginesStatus: failure and never emits the engines list, so state.engines stays [] and state.engine stays null. TranslatePage shows NoEnginesView ('no instance reachable / no AI provider'), which hides the engine selector. Retry calls loadEngines(refresh:true), which picks the same saved engine and fails the same way. selectEngine also persists the choice (_settings.setEngine at line 162) before the languages have loaded, so a single tap on a broken engine is enough to set this up for the next launch. Repro (confirmed): settings engineId 'mozhi:deepl', getSourceLanguages(deepl) throws, getEngines returns [google, deepl, claude], then loadEngines() twice. Result: engines isEmpty and engine null both times, although Google and Claude work. Real trigger: a Mozhi instance whose DeepL/Yandex backend is broken while /api/engines still lists it.
cubit.fix: In loadEngines, on a language failure fall back to the next candidate (state.engine, then the default, then the first engine) and log the error. If that also fails, still emit engines: engines (and engine) so the selector stays reachable. In _switchEngine, call _settings.setEngine only after the languages loaded successfully.

cubit.title: Smart swap on first run moves English text to Abkhaz/Afrikaans and saves it as the target
cubit.scenario: The defaults are source auto, target English and an empty recentLanguages list. The default target is never added to recents. An English speaker types 'Hello there' and the result is detected as 'en', which equals the target, so a smart swap runs. There are no usable recents, and the English fallback is skipped because the text is English. The code then returns the first entry of targetLanguages, which is alphabetical: 'ab' Abkhaz in LanguageCatalog.all (AI engines), or Afrikaans/Abkhaz for Mozhi Google. The output is in Abkhaz, and settings.setLanguages(target: ab) plus addRecentLanguage(ab) save it. Confirmed by repro: target.code == 'ab' after translate().
cubit.fix: Do not fall back to an arbitrary first list entry. Use a sensible preference order: recents, then the device/UI locale, then a short list of popular languages (es, fr, de, zh…) that exist in targets. If none applies, return null (no swap). Seeding recentLanguages with the initial target would also help.

Onboarding never calls it (grep finds no setLanguages or addRecentLanguage in lib/onboarding).

   - Lines 572-575: the English fallback is skipped because _primarySubtag('en') == 'en'.
   - Lines 576-578: `for (final language in targets) { if (differs(language)) return language; }` returns targets.first.

That list is sorted by English name and its first entry is `Language(code: 'ab', name: 'Abkhaz')` (language_catalog.dart:62). For Mozhi engines the list is whatever order the instance returns, usually alphabetical (Afrikaans or Abkhaz).

4. _onResult (lines 519-534) then saves the change with _settings.setLanguages(target: ab) and addRecentLanguage(ab), and translates again into Abkhaz. Abkhaz is now the saved target

cubit.title: swap() replaces the user's edited text with an outdated or half-streamed translation
cubit.scenario: swap() always moves state.output into the input. That result may belong to older text, because setInput keeps the old result, and a result from a request still in flight can arrive after an edit. It may also be a partial streaming snapshot. Repro (confirmed): state input 'Hello', result 'Hallo' (en->de). setInput('Hello world, how are you?') then swap() leaves input == 'Hallo'. The user's new sentence is discarded with no undo, and 'Hallo' is translated instead. This is reachable at any time for AI engines (instantTranslateAi is off by default), within the 600 ms debounce or request window for Mozhi engines, and while an AI stream is running (input becomes e.g. 'Hallo We').
cubit.fix: Use the output only when it is current: track the input or request the result was made for (store request.text with the result, or a resultIsCurrent flag cleared in setInput) and require result.isComplete with no translation in flight. Otherwise keep state.input and only swap the languages.

cubit.title: Choosing an engine during an engine refresh throws away the refreshed list and leaves enginesStatus stuck on 'loading'
cubit.scenario: A provider or instance change calls loadEngines(refresh:true), which emits enginesStatus.loading and waits on a slow Mozhi getEngines. Meanwhile the user picks an engine. _switchEngine increments _enginesRequest, so the refresh result is dropped, and _switchEngine itself never sets enginesStatus back to ready. Confirmed: after the refresh resolves with [google, deepl, claude, local], enginesStatus == loading and engines == the old list, so the AI provider the user just added never appears. waitForEngines (share intents, deep links) then waits the full 20 s timeout every time. Related: after a failed switch, a later successful switch leaves enginesStatus == failure (confirmed).
cubit.fix: In _switchEngine, emit enginesStatus: EnginesStatus.ready on success. proofread.title: locate() matches edit originals as raw substrings, so short originals land inside other words and corrupt the output
proofread.scenario: Input "Mary want a apple and a orange." with edits that are valid and in order: [want->wants, a->an, a->an] (the model gives the bare article as the original). After 'want' the cursor is at 9, so edit 1 matches the real 'a' at 10. Edit 2 then searches from 11, and the first 'a' it finds is the one in 'apple' at 12. Rejecting edit 0 makes outputText = apply(...) = "Mary want an anpple and a orange." I reproduced this with ProofreadDiff.apply. The inline diff highlights the 'a' inside 'apple', and the real 'a orange' is never fixed. A single edit is affected the same way: 'This is wrong.' with is->was gives 'Thwas is wrong.' whenever correctedText is missing or not used. Copy, Share and 'Use as input' then export the corrupted text.
proofread.fix: In locate(), prefer occurrences on token boundaries. If the original starts with a letter, mark or digit, require that the character before the match is not one; apply the same rule to the character after the match. Fall back to a plain substring match only when no boundary match exists after the cursor. Add tests with 'a', 'is' and 'an' originals.

The parser keeps both because both occur in the input. locate() starts its search for 'Teh' after 'mat', finds nothing and returns null. The tile for 'Teh->The' says "Couldn't match this edit to your text." even though 'Teh' is at index 0. If the user unchecks 'mat->rug', the output becomes "Teh cat sat on teh mat." (verified): the 'Teh->The' edit is still checked but has vanished. Overlapping edits such as 'teh cat' and 'cat sat' fail in the same way.

Return null only when the text truly cannot be placed.

proofread.title: Myers trace stores the full V array per step, so moderately long texts fall back to a whole-text replacement and the diff runs synchronously in build
proofread.scenario: On a 2000-word text with every 7th word changed (about 14%, typical for the 'comprehensive' level), wordDiff returns 4 segments, meaning the entire text is struck through and reinserted (verified). With every 10th word changed it takes about 0.9 s under JIT, run synchronously from _ProofreadResultCardState._segmentsFor during build. That path is the default view whenever all edits are accepted and correctedText != applied, and it also runs on 'Accept all', freezing the UI.
proofread.fix: Snapshot only the active band v[offset-d .. offset+d] (2d+1 cells) per step, so memory is O(D^2) instead of O(D*(N+M)), or use linear-space Myers. Run large diffs off the UI thread (compute/Isolate.run) or cache them in the cubit.

proofread.title: 'Comprehensive' correction-level label is truncated on standard 360 dp phones at default text size
proofread.scenario: At a 360x800 surface the 'Comprehensive' segment label gets 85 dp of width and didExceedMaxLines is true (verified in a widget test), so it renders as 'Comprehen…'. The segment tooltip shows the description, not the name, so sighted users cannot read the option name. With larger font scales the 'Standard' label truncates too.
proofread.fix: Allow 2 lines or use FittedBox(scaleDown) for segment labels, or move the SegmentedButton to a full-width row with a shorter label set. On narrow widths, fall back to the menu-button pattern used for style and formality.

proofread.title: Paste button replaces the whole input instead of inserting at the cursor, discarding typed text
proofread.scenario: The user types a paragraph, puts the cursor at the end and taps the always-visible Paste button to add a quote. _paste() calls setInput(clipboardText), and the listener overwrites the controller, so the whole paragraph is replaced by the clipboard text. On mobile there is no undo affordance.
proofread.fix: Insert the clipboard text at the controller's selection (replacing the selection if there is one) and then call setInput with the combined text. Alternatively, show Paste only when the input is empty.

proofread.title: Completed results and errors are not announced to screen readers
proofread.scenario: A TalkBack or VoiceOver user activates 'Proofread'. In the narrow layout the result or error card appears below the fold. Neither _ErrorCard, _NoIssuesCard nor the result card uses Semantics(liveRegion: true) or SemanticsService.announce, so the only feedback is the button label quietly changing back from 'Checking…' to 'Proofread'. A failure ('Couldn't proofread') or 'Looks good!' goes unannounced.
proofread.fix: Wrap the error card, the no-issues card and the result header in Semantics(liveRegion: true), or call SemanticsService.announce from a BlocListener on status transitions to success or failure.

proofread.title: Menu options do not expose which value is selected to assistive technology
proofread.scenario: In the Style, Formality and Model menus, the current option is shown only by a check Icon with no semanticLabel; unselected options get a transparent icon. Icons without a label are excluded from semantics, so a screen-reader user opening the menu hears 'General, Academic, Business…' with no 'selected' or 'checked' state on any of them.
proofread.fix: Wrap each MenuItemButton child in Semantics(selected: option == value, inMutuallyExclusiveGroup: true), or give the check icon a semanticLabel (e.g. l10n 'Selected') when option == value.

repo.title: Choosing a different preferred instance has no effect: the pool sticks to the instance it last used, even after the user reorders the list
repo.scenario: MozhiPool.run sets _preferred on every success, including the very first request to instances[0]. update() keeps _preferred as long as its URL is still in the list (lines 54-57). The 'Prefer instance' action in settings (SettingsCubit.preferInstance -> moveInstance(i, 0)) and onboarding's selectInstance / sort-by-speed both work only by reordering the list. Concretely: instances [A, B, C]; engines load from A at startup, so _preferred = A. The user taps 'Prefer' on C, so updateConfiguration([C, A, B]) runs, but activeInstance is still A. Every translate, getEngines(refresh: true), TTS and image call keeps going to A for the rest of the session. Reproduced in the pool (update([C,A,B]) leaves active == A) and in the repository (after reordering to [B, A], the engine subtitle is still 'Alpha' and the engines are fetched from A). This also has a privacy cost. A single engine-specific 5xx on the user's self-hosted instance (for example a Yandex captcha) moves the whole session to a public instance. The user cannot move back by reordering, and tapping Prefer on the instance already at index 0 does nothing at all. mozhi_pool_test.dart:205 ('keeps the preferred instance while it is configured') currently locks in this behaviour.
repo.fix: Treat the configured order as the user's intent. In update(), clear _preferred whenever the first instance changes (or whenever the order changes). Alternatively, only record _preferred when the success came from a failover (offset > 0), so a plain success on instances[0] does not pin it. Update the pool test at line 205 to match. A further option is a reset hook (for example clearing the preference on getEngines(refresh: true)) so the user can return to their primary instance.

repo.title: Instance-level HTTP failures (3xx/401/403/404/405/408/410) are treated as request errors, so the pool rethrows instead of failing over
repo.scenario: run() fails over only when MozhiApiException.isRetryable is true (no status, 429 or >= 500); any other status is rethrown immediately. Mozhi itself returns 400 only for missing parameters, and engine or language errors come back as 500. Every other 4xx/3xx comes from a dead, moved or protected instance. dart:io does not follow 301/302/307/308 redirects for POST, and the client turns them into 'Redirected to ...' errors with status 301. Example: the first default public instance moves to https or a new domain, or starts answering /api/* with 403 (WAF or bot protection) or 404 (parked domain or older Mozhi without the endpoint). Every translate, compare batch, TTS and image call then fails with that error, even though 10 other configured instances work. For 403/404, getEngines also rethrows on the first instance and returns only AI engines (or throws when none are configured). Reproduced: run() over [A, B] where A throws MozhiApiException(statusCode: 301) rethrows without trying B.
repo.fix: In MozhiPool.run, fail over on every status except request-specific ones: rethrow only for 400 (and perhaps 413/422). That means treating 3xx, 401, 403, 404, 405, 408, 410, 421 and 451 as instance failures. Or widen MozhiApiException.isRetryable in mozhi_api in the same way. Add pool tests for 301/403/404.

repo.title: Compare batch: an empty or partial 200 response is reported as per-engine failures with no failover, while single-engine translate would fail over
repo.scenario: Upstream Mozhi's TranslateSome (libmozhi engines.go:480) drops failed engines silently and returns HTTP 200 with [] or a partial array. A single-engine /api/translate for the same failure returns 500 and fails over. Its goroutines also append to a shared slice without a lock, so successful results can be lost at random. runMozhiBatch accepts any 200 from the first instance and reports missing engines as 'X returned no result.' Example: instances [A, B]; A's upstream Google and DeepL are rate-limited, so A answers [] with 200. compare([google, deepl]) shows both as failures, while translate(google) alone would fail over to B and succeed. Reproduced: with A returning [] and B returning both results, both CompareEntry values are failures.
repo.fix: Inside the _mozhi.run action, throw a retryable MozhiApiException when the response contains none of the requested engines, so the pool tries the next instance. For engines still missing from a partial response, run them individually through _translateMozhi, which has failover, before reporting a failure. Optionally do the same when the batch itself fails with a 5xx, to cover older instances that cannot handle comma lists.

repo.title: In-flight request whose instance is removed or replaced fails with 'Client is already closed' instead of trying the new instance list
repo.scenario: run() captures `instances = _instances` at the start. If updateConfiguration replaces the list while a request is in flight (for example 'Reset to defaults', or onboarding adding the user's own instance), update() closes the old client and the request fails with a retryable error. The loop then skips every captured instance that is no longer configured and never visits newly added ones, so it throws 'HTTP request failed. Client is already closed.' to the user. Reproduced: run over [A, B]; during A's request call update([C]) and throw the closed-client error. The run throws, and C is never tried.
repo.fix: After a retryable failure, re-read _instances and continue with configured instances that have not been tried yet, including new ones. Or, when the failure was caused by the client being closed (the instance was removed), restart from the current active instance.

repo.title: Engine and language caches are keyed by the instance active before failover, so they can later serve another instance's list
repo.scenario: _loadMozhiEngines and _mozhiLanguages compute the cache key from _mozhi.active before run() executes. If run() fails over, the result from instance B is stored under A's key. Example: [A, B]; A's /api/engines returns 502, B answers {deepl}, and the list is cached under A. Later B goes down and a translate fails back over to A, so active becomes A. getEngines() then hits A's key and returns B's engines (subtitle 'b.example', engine set from B) without ever fetching A's list. The same applies to source and target language lists. Reproduced: the subtitle is 'b.example' and the id is mozhi:deepl, although active is A and A would answer {google}.
repo.fix: Cache under the URL of the instance that actually answered: inside the run action, return the instance with the result and write cache[instance.url]. Or re-key the entry after completion, and on lookup verify that the cached instance equals the current active one.

repo.title: A trailing [[lang:xx]] marker is shown half-typed in intermediate snapshots
repo.scenario: splitLanguageMarker accepts a marker on the last line, but the stream's hold-back only uses isMarkerPending, which handles a leading marker and returns false as soon as the text contains a newline. When a model ends with the marker, as the parser explicitly tolerates, it usually arrives as several tokens, and the intermediate snapshot shows it. Deltas ['Hallo', '\n[[lang:', 'en]]'] with an auto source emit a snapshot 'Hallo\n[[lang:' (isComplete: false), visible to the user until the marker completes or for at least one throttle interval. This contradicts 'the marker is ... never shown'. Reproduced with snapshotInterval zero.
repo.fix: Before building an intermediate snapshot, strip a trailing partial marker on the last line (an unfinished '[', '[[', '[[l...', '[[lang:xx' suffix, matched with the same prefix-completion idea as isMarkerPending), or hold back the last line while it could still become a trailing marker. The final result already handles complete markers correctly.
